coordinates.note: No official KamLAND page or paper consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states numeric coordinates. This is the Wikipedia coordinate, so it is shown as a campus-grade, approximate point and not as an underground-laboratory position. KamLAND occupies the original Kamiokande cavity in the Kamioka mine, the same general underground complex as the Kamioka Observatory's primary site at Mozumi (Super-Kamiokande).

depth.locator: Sec. III (Cosmic-ray muons), Phys. Rev. C 81, 025807
depth.note: Vertical overburden under the peak of Ikenoyama; the paper gives the minimum overburden separately.
depth.quote: The vertical overburden at KamLAND is approximately 1000 m of rock

depth_mwe.note: Same Ikenoyama overburden as the Super-Kamiokande cavern record (2700 m.w.e.). Mei & Hime 2006, Table I, derive an equivalent flat-overburden depth of 2.05 ± 0.15 km.w.e. from the earlier KamLAND flux.
depth_mwe.quote: the vertical rock overburden is approximately 2700 meters water equivalent (mwe)

muon_flux.display: 1.49 × 10⁻⁷ cm⁻² s⁻¹ (± 0.11; published as 5.37 ± 0.41 m⁻² h⁻¹)
muon_flux.locator: Sec. III (Cosmic-ray muons), Phys. Rev. C 81, 025807
muon_flux.note: KamLAND's measured muon rate through its liquid scintillator, 0.198 ± 0.014 Hz (muon bundles estimated at < 5%), expressed by the paper as an integrated muon intensity of 5.37 ± 0.41 m^-2 h^-1; 5.37 m^-2 h^-1 is 1.49 × 10^-7 cm^-2 s^-1. The paper states no reference surface; the numbers match the rate divided by the 132.7 m^2 cross section of a sphere of 650 cm radius (its impact-parameter cut). Carried by the KamLAND site because it is the only measurement at Kamioka; the Super-Kamiokande cavern lies under the same mountain and has none of its own. The Hyper-Kamiokande design report (Table XXIX) gives a calculated (MUSIC) 1.54 × 10^-7 cm^-2 s^-1 for Super-K, which it says agrees with this measurement. Mei & Hime Table I lists an earlier KamLAND report, (1.58 ± 0.21) × 10^-7; Woodley et al. 2024 Table III lists (1.49 ± 0.11) × 10^-7 for KamLAND (2010).
muon_flux.quote: The muon rate corresponds to an integrated muon intensity of Jµ = 5.37 ± 0.41 m−2 h−1

name: KamLAND cavity, Kamioka mine
notes: Wikipedia states an overburden of '105 m.w.e.' for KamLAND. This is inconsistent with the ~2700 m.w.e. given for the same Kamioka mine by the Kamioka Observatory record and by the KamLAND collaboration's own muon paper (Phys. Rev. C 81, 025807), and is very likely a Wikipedia error or a different overburden metric. It is deliberately not recorded; depth, water-equivalent depth and muon flux below come from the KamLAND paper.

summary.plain: The cavern in the Kamioka mine in Japan, originally dug for the first Kamiokande detector, that now holds the KamLAND reactor-antineutrino detector.
summary.technical: Underground cavity within the Kamioka mine (facility:kamioka-observatory), reusing the original Kamiokande excavation, housing the KamLAND liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector.
